 with many mo] ‘The sense, of course, is, not “As Spenser and many others say,” but “This and

Ah for loue of that, is to thee moste leefe,
Hobbinol, I pray thee gall not my old griefe:
Sike question ripeth vp cause of newe woe,
For one opened mote vnfolde many moe.
 The Spenserian ‘moe’ is used in Byron, Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage I lciii 4. See Davie, Purity 141: ‘The

its ungainly self.’
